semantic_contract: Given a container in ECX and a pointer to a 32-bit key in the single callee-cleaned stack argument, walks the container's red-black tree from the anchor's parent slot (receiver + 0x0c) with an unsigned key comparison at node + 0x10 - left when node->key < *key, right and record the candidate otherwise - and returns the ADDRESS of the mapped value at node + 0x14 when the recorded candidate satisfies *key >= candidate->key, i.e. when the search stopped on a node whose key is not greater than the searched one. The tree is ordered ascending, the left subtree holds the larger keys, and an empty container skips the descent entirely. When the key is absent - the candidate is still the anchor, or the candidate's key is strictly greater than *key - the function calls one out-of-line insert helper at 0x0059c520 with four arguments: the address of a caller-owned 4-byte cell, the lower-bound candidate as a hint, the address of a private copy of *key, and the key pointer with its low byte cleared; it then reads the resulting node pointer back out of that cell and returns node + 0x14, so both paths return the address of a mapped 4-byte handle. The function never returns null, never dereferences the container when the key argument is null on the hit path but does dereference it unconditionally on the miss path, and touches no global.
classification_rationale: The complete 51-instruction body, the __thiscall + RET 0x4 ABI, the frame, the node and container offsets, the unsigned comparison polarity, both branch polarities, both exits, the four-argument port call and the port's arg1 write are all read directly from the disassembly, and the model test pins the hit path, the three distinct miss shapes (empty container, key above every entry, key between entries), the ascending order and the unsigned comparison. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because material elements remain bounded: (1) the OWNING TYPE of the container and of the mapped value is inferred from the Spore-ModAPI header, not from the binary - there is no RTTI and no vtable was located, so 'eastl::map<int, EditorCreatureControllerPtr>' inside cEditorAnimWorld is a corroborated label and not an established identity; (2) the insert helper 0x0059c520 is kept as an opaque port, so what the inserted node's mapped value is initialised to, and whether the insert can fail, are not established; (3) the purpose of the key-pointer masking (& 0xffffff00, passed as argument 4 and dereferenced as a pointer inside 0x0059c520 at 0x0059c59c) is unexplained, so the port contract is bounded even though its instruction sequence is not.
semantic_findings: This is a find-or-create accessor over an ascending integer-keyed associative container: a lower-bound descent plus an out-of-line insert on the miss path, returning the address of the mapped value.

The order is ascending, not descending: the JC at 0x0059c75b sends the search left when node->key < *key, so the left subtree holds the larger keys. 0x0059c380 walks the same tree with the identical polarity, which is what fixes the direction; reading the branches the other way round would make it a descending map.
The key comparison is unsigned (JC/JNC with no sign extension), confirmed by the 0x0059c758 encoding and pinned by model test 8.
The return value is a pointer to the mapped 4-byte handle, not the handle: three call sites dereference it once, and one hands it to another method as ECX.

The container layout is read directly (anchor at +0x04, root at +0x0c, count at +0x14, 0x1c bytes total) and matches the eastl::map header that the Spore-ModAPI places at cEditorAnimWorld+0x08, field for field, including the owner's +0x38/+0x3c/+0x40 pointers.

The presence test *key >= candidate->key after a lower-bound walk means an exact match in a unique-key container; a candidate whose key is strictly greater is a miss even though it is the lower bound.
An empty container takes the miss path with the anchor itself as the hint - the walk is skipped entirely at 0x0059c754.

The compiler reuses the function's own incoming argument slot as the insert helper's out-parameter, and the same cell supplies the helper's fourth argument after its low byte is cleared. Both facts are instruction-level observations.
All 22 references are direct calls and the address is in no vtable, so this is a template instantiation body, not an interface method - consistent with the SDK's descriptor naming.
unresolved_questions: What is the mapped element type? The binary shows a 4-byte handle whose target has a pointer at +0x08 whose vtable slot +0x04 is called (0x0059cb5a..0x0059cb6d). 'EditorCreatureControllerPtr' comes from the SDK header and is not proven.

Why is the low byte of the key pointer cleared (0x0059c77b) and the result passed as argument 4, and why does 0x0059c520 dereference it at 0x0059c59c? It is used only on a path that a non-empty container can reach, and the dereference reads the caller's own stack page, so the value compared there is not the searched key. This is unexplained and is the weakest part of the reconstruction.

Does the container really use eastl::map with the default comparator? The 0x1c-byte header shape and the anchor convention match, but no vtable or typeinfo record was located and the allocator at +0x18 was never read.

What value does 0x0059c520 give a freshly inserted node's mapped handle - null, or something else? The helper is an opaque port here, so operator[]-style default initialisation is assumed but not observed.
Can the insert fail or assert? 0x0059c520 has no visible failure return; EAX is set on every path, but no error path was identified.

Call site 0x0059c981 can pass a null key pointer (0x0059c972 XOR EDI,EDI). On the miss path this body dereferences it unconditionally (0x0059c775), so that path would fault. Whether the container is guaranteed empty there, or whether the null never reaches this call, is not established statically.

Are the 22 callers all operating on the same container instance, or does 0x0059c740 serve several containers of this instantiation? Only the four named editor callers were traced to cEditorAnimWorld+0x08.
The other 18 call sites (FUN_0059c830 .. FUN_0059d300) were not individually disassembled; their receiver and key setup is assumed to match the four that were read.
